title: Sample 15-3: Line-Numbered Prose with Transcriber’s Note

illustrates.quote: d. On the Transcriber’s Notes page, inform the reader about the function of the three blank cells when line-numbered prose occurs in more than one section in a volume. Insert a transcriber’s note before the text when the three blank cells is used in only one section. Sample: Three blank cells occurring within a braille line indicate the beginning of a new print line.

blocks.text: It rained all afternoon in a single tone. In the uniform and peaceful
intensity you could hear the water fall, the way it is when you travel all
afternoon on a train. But without our noticing it, the rain was pene-
trating too deeply into our senses. Early Monday morning, when we
closed the door to avoid the cutting, icy draft that blew in from the
courtyard, our senses had been filled with rain. And on Monday

print.notes: Print numbers only lines 1 and 5 in the left margin; the other four blocks' 'number' fields are the actual sequential print-line numbers, confirmed by direct decode of the given braille's own right-margin digits (#a=1 ... #f=6). No explicit transcriber's-note print.blocks entry is modeled here on purpose: the note shown in the gold braille below ("Three blank cells occurring... new print line.") is this rule's own SUGGESTED wording (15.4.1d's own 'Sample:' text), not a note this particular worked excerpt's own surrounding prose independently supplies — it exists ONLY because Emboss's pipeline is expected to insert ITS OWN automatic transcriber's note (document.mjs's hardcoded LINE_NUMBER_NOTE) before the first line-numbered block of any document. Leaving this file's print.blocks as prose-only (no manual note block) is what correctly tests that automatic mechanism against the book's own worked illustration of exactly what such a note should say.

resolution: Braille unchanged (A and B agree, already verified verbatim). The transcriber's note text itself is NOT modeled as a print.blocks entry (see 'notes' above) so that Emboss's own automatic §15.4.1d note (LINE_NUMBER_NOTE, document.mjs:737) is what gets compared against this rule's own worked example of the correct wording — expect a wording mismatch (Emboss's fixed text differs word-for-word from the book's own suggested text, though both convey the same three-blank-cell convention); if not already covered by an existing finding this reconciliation records it as a new one (see differences.md).
